entity: Groupon, Inc. — US employing entity (Groupon Management LLC or similar; to confirm)
summary: No federal vacation law. Chicago staff get two separate hour banks — Paid Leave and Paid Sick Leave — with different waiting periods, carry-over caps and payout rules. Work location, not entity, decides which law applies.

locationAssumption.citation: Chicago Ord. 6-130 applies to employees working ≥80h in any 120-day period physically in Chicago; Illinois PLAWA (820 ILCS 192) exempts employers covered by the Chicago ordinance — non-Chicago Illinois staff need a separate PLAWA pack
locationAssumption.note: 820 ILCS 192/15 and 56 Ill. Adm. Code 200.270 confirm the exemption. OLS says coverage is 80 hours in any 120 days in Chicago; an older Clerk draft says 2 hours in any 2-week period — counsel to confirm the codified text.

rule.citation: Leave is taken in hours of the scheduled shift; employers may set minimum increments of 4 hours (Paid Leave) and 2 hours (Paid Sick Leave) and require up to 7 days' notice for foreseeable Paid Leave

source.citation: Groupon US company holiday calendar (no private-sector statutory holidays in Illinois)
source.note: Calendar is a placeholder (no public Groupon US holiday list exists); all dates match OPM federal holiday observance rules.

rule.citation: Company holidays are paid days off outside the leave banks (policy assumption)
Chicago Ord. 6-130 Paid Leave: 1h per 35h worked, max 40h per year; usable from day 90
Chicago Ord. 6-130: 1 hour per 35 hours worked, up to 40 hours per 12-month period (accrual method assumed; front-loading is also permitted)
rule.note: Accrual year assumed to be the calendar year. Exempt employees are deemed to work 40 hours a week; only hours worked in Chicago accrue.

rule.citation: Chicago Ord. 6-130: carry-over of up to 16 hours into the next 12-month period
Employee may use Paid Sick Leave for own illness; paid-leave hours for those days are restored and sick hours debited
rule.note: Ordinance silent on vacation interruption; this is a proposed Groupon policy.

rule.citation: Chicago Ord. 6-130: unused accrued Paid Leave is paid out on separation (or transfer out of Chicago) by employers with more than 100 Chicago covered employees — 51–100 were capped at 16 hours until 1 July 2025, now full; 50 or fewer owe nothing
rule.note: Checked against the City Clerk ordinance text and Office of Labor Standards rules. Only Chicago-based employees count toward the thresholds.

rule.citation: Chicago Ord. 6-130 Paid Sick Leave: 1h per 35h worked, max 40h per year; usable from day 30
Chicago Ord. 6-130: 1 hour per 35 hours worked, up to 40 hours per 12-month period (accrual method assumed; front-loading is also permitted)
rule.note: Accrual year assumed to be the calendar year.

rule.citation: Chicago Ord. 6-130: carry-over of up to 80 hours into the next 12-month period
Not applicable to the sick bank
Chicago Ord. 6-130: unused Paid Sick Leave is never paid out

extras.label: FMLA
extras.citation: FMLA 29 U.S.C. 2601 et seq.: up to 12 workweeks unpaid job-protected leave (eligibility 12 months / 1,250 hours)

extras.label: Groupon PTO surplus
extras.citation: Illinois Wage Payment and Collection Act 820 ILCS 115/5 and 56 Ill. Adm. Code 300.520: earned vacation is final compensation and must be paid on separation; use-it-or-lose-it is allowed only with notice and a reasonable opportunity to take it
extras.note: Need the actual US PTO policy. Built In (third-party, updated Sept 2026) describes it as "unlimited or flexible PTO" — if confirmed, set paid-leave accrual to unlimited-with-floor.

extras.label: Unlimited PTO option
extras.citation: Chicago Ord. 6-130-030(g): an unlimited PTO policy satisfies the ordinance, needs no carry-over, but on separation or transfer out of Chicago the employer pays 40 hours minus the hours used in the 12 months before separation
extras.note: Groupon's own postings say "flexible PTO" (Dallas); third-party profiles say "unlimited or flexible" — unconfirmed. Switch Paid Leave to unlimited-with-floor on the Rule packs page to model it. Sick-leave protections still apply, so the engine keeps the sick bank separate.

extras.label: One combined bank
extras.citation: Chicago OLS Rule PTO 2.08 (rules effective 1 June 2026): an employer may run one paid-time-off policy of up to 80 hours that meets or exceeds every requirement of 6-130-030 instead of two banks
extras.note: The engine models two banks, the default. How carry-over works in a combined bank is not spelled out.
